To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CK1ϵ regulates the period of the circadian pacemaker via its phosphorylation of PER1 and/or PER2, but does not regulate the period via PER3.
CK1ϵ regulates the period of the molecular pacemaker via phosphorylation of PER1 or PER 2 proteins, with PER1 and PER3 being dispensable.
the Tau mutation of casein kinase 1 epsilon (CKIϵ) sets the period of the mammalian circadian pacemaker via regulation of both Period1 (Per1) and Period2 (Per2) clock proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that underlie circadian rhythms, and how they are affected by human disease.
the molecular mechanisms that underlie the circadian pacemaker, which is a group of brain cells that generates the daily cycle of sleep and rest.
understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying circadian rhythm generation in the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CK1ϵ is required for the normal functioning of both PER1 and, especially, PER2 in the SCN, and that PER1 and PER3 are the principal substrates of the enzyme in this tissue.

CK1ϵ regulates the period of the mammalian molecular clock via PER1 and PER3, but not PER2, and that CK1ϕ Tau accelerates circadian rhythms by increasing the degradation rate of PER1 and, to a lesser extent, PER2.
the Tau mutation of hCK1ϵ is a period-accelerator of the SCN molecular oscillator via its actions on the PER1 and PER 2 proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CK1ϵ is a critical regulator of mammalian circadian timing and its period, and that the Tau mutation accelerates circadian period in a PER1- and PER2-dependent manner.

CK1ϵ has divergent actions in vivo and in SCN slices, acting via PER1 and PER 2 to regulate circadian period, and that the PER-independent cellular oscillators that are observed in SCN slices are not affected by CK1ϵ.
PER proteins are the primary substrates of CK-1ϵ, but the Tau allele can accelerate the period of the mammalian pacemaker in the absence of both PER1 and 2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CK1ϵ is a key regulator of circadian rhythms and that CK1ϲTau mice provide a useful tool to study how CK1ϵ affects circadian pacemakers.
CK1ϵ regulates the period of the mammalian circadian pacemaker by phosphorylating and destabilizing PER1 or PER 2, but not both, in vivo.

CK1ϵ has a dual function in the circadian clock: it phosphorylates PER proteins to accelerate the molecular clock, but it also phosphorylates other proteins to regulate the amplitude and stability of circadian oscillations.
